words.sense: indirectly suggest an unpleasant accusation or criticism
misconceptions: An indirect suggestion is not automatically an attack.

words.sense: communicate a neutral or other meaning without saying it outright
misconceptions: An indirect accusation carries a negative charge beyond a neutral inference.

semantic_axes.description: To insinuate is to suggest something unpleasant or accusatory indirectly; to imply is simply to communicate something indirectly.

edges.boundary_rule: To insinuate is to suggest something unpleasant or accusatory indirectly; to imply is simply to communicate something indirectly.

misconceptions.M1: An indirect suggestion is not automatically an attack.
misconceptions.M2: An indirect accusation carries a negative charge beyond a neutral inference.
misconceptions.M3: Do not stick with an old answer after decisive evidence changes, or let surface distractions override the boundary.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what Nabil communicated?

beats.text: Nabil looked at a missing receipt and remarked that some people were oddly comfortable handling club money alone.
beats.decisive_clue: indirect suspicion of dishonest handling of money
beats.reason: The statement casts doubt on someone’s integrity without an open accusation.

beats.text: He made the remark while staring at the treasurer who had last handled the cash box.
beats.decisive_clue: indirect suspicion directed at a particular person
beats.reason: His attention to the treasurer sharpens the negative suggestion.

chains.feedback_short: The key is indirect suspicion directed at a particular person; his attention to the treasurer sharpens the negative suggestion.
chains.feedback_deep: Insinuate concerns indirectly suggest an unpleasant accusation or criticism; imply concerns communicate a neutral or other meaning without saying it outright. His attention to the treasurer sharpens the negative suggestion.
chains.contrast_rule: Insinuate: unstated accusation of cheating; imply: unstated timing information.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what Aziz communicated?

beats.text: Aziz said the highest score was surprising and wondered whether one student had received private access to the answer sheets.
beats.decisive_clue: a veiled suspicion of improper access to answer sheets
beats.reason: By wondering aloud about private access, he indirectly casts suspicion on the student's result.

beats.text: He delivered the remark in a friendly voice.
beats.decisive_clue: the same veiled suspicion of improper advantage
beats.reason: A friendly tone does not remove the accusation embedded in the remark.

chains.feedback_short: The key is a veiled suspicion of improper access; a friendly tone does not remove the accusation embedded in the remark.
chains.feedback_deep: Insinuate indirectly suggests an unpleasant accusation or criticism; imply communicates a meaning indirectly without necessarily making an accusation. Wondering aloud about private access casts suspicion on the student's result, and a friendly tone does not remove that accusation.
chains.contrast_rule: Insinuate: an indirect accusation of cheating; imply: an indirect neutral meaning such as timing or readiness.

beats.text: Greta said the shop lights would be turned off in ten minutes while a customer browsed.
beats.decisive_clue: a closing-time message conveyed without a direct command
beats.reason: Her words indirectly ask the customer to finish.

beats.text: She placed a shopping basket by the checkout as she spoke.
beats.decisive_clue: a closing-time message supported by checkout preparation
beats.reason: The basket reinforces the practical message; no one’s character is attacked.
